Messages.Author: Jon Stahler
Messages.Body:
Does it still mean tapped in torpor and doesn't untap as normal? Is it still
free to rescue a paralyzed vamp? What about untapping when out of torpor?
Does it occur as normal? Thanks in advance for the answers.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Jon Stahler wrote:
>
> Does [Paralyze] still mean tapped in torpor and doesn't untap as normal? Is it

> still free to rescue a paralyzed vamp? What about untapping when out of torpor?
> Does it occur as normal? Thanks in advance for the answers.

Paralyze doesn't mean anything anymore - the term is not used in V:TES any
longer. Its meaning was not changed prior to being dropped, however.

Messages.Author: Gomi no Sensei
Messages.Body:
In article <B%wM6.6269$ki5....@vixen.cso.uiuc.edu>,


Paralyze no longer exists as a concept in V:tES, and all cards referring to
it are banned in tournament play. Note, however, that as a practical matter
this means only Rowan Ring, as Stake uses the text for Wooden Stake (Sabbat):

"Melee Weapon. Strength damage each strike. If more than 1 damage is inflicted
on an opposing vampire by this weapon in a given combat, then that vampire is
sent into torpor. In that case, this card is transferred to that vampire, and
he or she doesn't untap as normal during the untap phase as long as he or she
remains in torpor."

As a house rule, you could use Rowan Ring with a modified version of the same
text:

"Unique Weapon. If at close range, bearer may strike to send the opposing
vampire into torpor. In that case, this card is transferred to that vampire,
and he or she doesn't untap as normal during the untap phase as long as he or
she remains in torpor."
